papers.title: TRACE: Accountable Agentic Retrieval for Source Discovery in Digital Archives
papers.authors: Donghan Bian, Marie Puren, Florian Cafiero
papers.summary: A training-free agentic retrieval framework for heterogeneous, OCR-degraded archives with strict source traceability. On 1,752 questions it reports R@10 of 0.856 and MRR of 0.653, outperforming sparse, dense, graph-based, and agentic RAG baselines at about $0.02 per query.
papers.use: The problem structure is unusually close to OncoGraph: multi-hop retrieval across heterogeneous corpora where provenance matters. It suggests that corpus-aware agent design may add more value than heavier graph construction or retraining.
papers.steal: Log source provenance and query reformulation at every retrieval step, then stratify failures by multi-hop, cross-corpus, and noisy-source conditions.
papers.doubt: Historical-archive gains may not transfer to biomedical entity normalization or directed relations. OncoGraph must also evaluate edge support, contradiction, and temporal validity.

papers.title: TorchCraft: Unified binder design by inverting an all-atom structure predictor
papers.authors: Yu Liu, Zhouhanyu Shen, Zhengyi Li, Xikun Huang, Jiaqi Liu, Shuxian Gao, Qilin Yu, Xiayan Qin, Yucheng Zhang, Mingchen Chen
papers.summary: Optimizes sequence logits through a frozen all-atom structure predictor, combining confidence, contact, geometry, and sequence priors in one procedure. Using AlphaFold 3 weights, it reports experimentally measured binding for representative minibinders and VHHs across four targets per format.
papers.use: This is a strong example of reusing a learned world model as an inverse-design engine rather than retraining it. It offers a formal template for designing interventions from a network-biology world model.
papers.steal: Freeze the predictor and optimize soft inputs against multiple physical and geometric objectives, avoiding a separate generator.
papers.doubt: The abstract does not reveal the denominator behind the experimental successes. A prospective blinded panel is needed to distinguish true design ability from favorable selection.

papers.title: SCGFM-ART: Amortized Relational Transport for Structure-Centric Graph Foundation Models
papers.authors: Xiaodong He, Xincheng Wang, Zhao Kang
papers.summary: Aligns heterogeneous graphs to a shared relational atlas using amortized graph-to-basis transport. Across 14 cross-domain tasks it reports strong transfer and 44–85× faster frozen target-domain inference than iterative alignment.
papers.use: It could place OncoGraph, cell-cell networks, and perturbation graphs into common coordinates based on structural roles rather than node identity—a graph analogue of Transfer Trust.
papers.steal: Separate global graph coordinates from local node-to-role correspondences, and use transport confidence as a signal for whether transfer should be trusted.
papers.doubt: Classification ranks do not guarantee useful biomedical link prediction or evidence retrieval. Atlas interpretability and coverage on out-of-domain graphs need direct testing.

papers.title: A Learning Algorithm for Threshold Boolean Networks with Prescribed Fixed Points
papers.summary: Learns threshold Boolean networks with a loss that preserves desired fixed points, penalizes spurious attractors, encourages binary outputs, and promotes sparsity. On an Arabidopsis GRN, five of 30 runs recovered all ten desired fixed points with no spurious ones.
papers.use: This is a simple but clear way to define a closed biological world as an attractor set. It suggests evaluating not only recovered biological states but also false stable states introduced by a model.
papers.steal: Separate desired-attractor recall from spurious-attractor count and constrain network sparsity in the same objective.
papers.doubt: Perfect recovery occurs in only five of 30 runs on one small GRN. Scalability to stochastic, asynchronous, larger networks is unknown.

papers.title: Labeled Incidence Structures for Native Transformer Modeling of Text, Knowledge Graphs, and Hypergraphs
papers.summary: Represents text, knowledge graphs, and hypergraphs uniformly as content-role-relation-instance triples instead of flattening them into sequences. Relative transport gives attention a role- and relation-aware structural bias.
papers.use: This directly addresses structural loss when OncoGraph triples are serialized for an LLM. Drug-target-disease-evidence tuples could remain one relation instance with explicit endpoint roles.
papers.steal: Give every endpoint a content value, slot, and relation-instance address, then define attention through role-aware relative transport.
papers.doubt: The work is theory-heavy, and the abstract does not establish gains over graph transformers or serialization baselines at realistic KG scale.

papers.title: Integrating knowledge from case reports: a medical ontology based multimodal information system with structured summary
papers.authors: Shuyu Guo, Lan Huang, Yichen Liu, Hanbin Ma, Tian Bai
papers.summary: Structures 52,949 open-access medical case reports into patient summaries, images, and biomedical entities organized through a medical ontology, with an interface for rare-disease case retrieval.
papers.use: It offers a data-model example for adding case-level evidence to OncoGraph while preserving patients, findings, treatments, outcomes, and images rather than only paper-level edges.
papers.steal: Preserve a paper-to-case-to-patient-timeline hierarchy and make the structured case summary a first-class evidence object.
papers.doubt: The abstract does not report extraction accuracy or quantitative retrieval and diagnostic gains. System scale should not be mistaken for validated research impact.

papers.title: Physical knowledge on historical data matters more than enforcing physical constraints on the forecast
papers.authors: Etienne Lehembre, Pascal Audigane, Vincent Nguyen, Christel Vrain, Thi-Bich-Hanh Dao
papers.summary: Predicts unobserved physical variables over both historical and forecast windows instead of enforcing physics only on future outputs. On groundwater data it performs best on five of 12 datasets and receives expert review of latent-variable coherence.
papers.use: A biological world model may be more robust if it reconstructs latent mechanisms throughout historical trajectories rather than only constraining endpoints.
papers.steal: Add an auxiliary objective that reconstructs latent mechanisms over the observed history, not only the forecast.
papers.doubt: Winning five of 12 datasets is not universal superiority, and expert plausibility of unobserved variables does not establish identifiability.

papers.title: Rethinking Multi-Agent Collaboration: When More Is Less
papers.authors: Yishuo Yuan, Yibo Wu, Yihan Zhang, Minyuan Sun, Shenliang Li, Xinkai Ma, Yifan Li, Jiaheng Liu
papers.summary: Finds that multi-agent collaboration helps mainly on long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies, while single-agent harnesses remain better for tightly coupled sequential workflows. SAIGE spawns agents on demand using an evolving semantic dependency graph.
papers.use: This supports parallelizing loosely coupled research tasks such as ingestion and benchmark generation while keeping tightly coupled manuscript consistency under one owner.
papers.steal: Estimate task-dependency sparsity and spawn agents on demand rather than fixing the team size.
papers.doubt: The system's own semantic retrieval determines task coupling, so bad decomposition may itself drive failure. Compare against human-specified dependencies.

papers.title: Parallelism, critical windows, and separations among diffusion language models
papers.summary: Provides a theoretical comparison of parallel sampling in masked, uniform, and Gaussian diffusion language models. It relates forward-pass complexity to dual total correlation and proves a distribution family where uniform and Gaussian diffusion asymptotically outperform masked diffusion.
papers.use: It replaces the vague claim that diffusion is parallel with a framework based on the dependency structure of the target distribution and its critical sampling windows.
papers.steal: Compare generative models through intrinsic dependency measures and required forward passes rather than sequence length alone.
papers.doubt: The 90-page theory may not translate to finite biomedical sequences or practical score approximations; constants and approximation error matter.

papers.title: Improving Generalization and Robustness in Offline Reinforcement Learning via Boundary-Aware Data Augmentation
papers.authors: Gong Gao, Weidong Zhao, Xianhui Liu
papers.summary: Shows that random episode interpolation error grows with state distance and proposes boundary-aware augmentation using neighboring states. It aims to preserve multimodal value distributions and improve robustness in limited-data offline RL.
papers.use: The same warning applies to perturbation mixup: unconstrained interpolation can create biologically impossible states. Augmentation should remain within local support.
papers.steal: Define interpolation regions through local neighbor boundaries and explicitly test whether synthetic samples collapse multimodal targets.
papers.doubt: RL state distance may reflect useful locality, whereas single-cell latent or drug-space distance may not. That assumption requires direct falsification.
